title: Closure of the Isthmus of Panama
summary: Between three and 2.8 million years ago, the tectonic uplift and emergence of the Isthmus of Panama severed the Central American Seaway between the Atlantic and Pacific oceans. This land bridge rerouted ocean currents to form the modern Gulf Stream, profoundly influencing global climate, while enabling the Great American Biotic Interchange of terrestrial mammals and plants between North and South America and permanently isolating marine populations.

uncertainty.note: Traditional geological and palaeontological consensus dates the complete emergence of the isthmus to between 3.0 and 2.8 Ma; disputed earlier shoaling and island-arc connections date to the Miocene.

as_recorded.value: By about 3 million years ago, an isthmus had formed between North and South America
formation of the Isthmus of Panama sensu stricto around 2.8 Ma

where.historical_name: Central American land bridge between the Pacific Ocean and the Caribbean Sea; no human polities existed

importance.justification: Severed the Atlantic and Pacific oceans, reorganized global ocean circulation to form the Gulf Stream, and triggered the Great American Biotic Interchange.

related.because: The megafauna involved in the late Pleistocene American extinctions descended from the interchange across the Panama isthmus.

beats.caption: Tectonic collision and sediment build-up gradually close the marine gap between the Americas.
Complete closure establishes the Gulf Stream and triggers the Great American Biotic Interchange.
